correctness.rationale: For q,r∈H2, q overline(r) has harmonic degrees 0,2,4. Second-moment isotropy kills the H2 center average, and normalized Funk–Hecke coefficient a4(c)=c(1+c)(7c²−3)/8 kills H4 exactly at sqrt(3/7), leaving constant mean. The tetrahedral 2-design with q=x²−y² has ∑q(u)²=0 but spherical mean 4/15, so degree-four moment −4/15 is nonzero and proves unique universal c in (0,1). Exact symbolic Legendre polynomial integration and tetrahedral witness independently checked. Quantifier covers all probability measures, not a numerical finite sample.
